rows.name: auth_rls_initplan
rows.title: Auth RLS Initialization Plan
rows.description: Detects if calls to \`current_setting()\` and \`auth.<function>()\` in RLS policies are being unnecessarily re-evaluated for each row
rows.detail: Table \`public.memberships\` has a row level security policy \`memberships_select\` that re-evaluates current_setting() or auth.<function>() for each row. This produces suboptimal query performance at scale. Resolve the issue by replacing \`auth.<function>()\` with \`(select auth.<function>())\`. See [docs](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security#call-functions-with-select) for more info.

rows.name: rls_disabled_in_public
rows.title: RLS Disabled in Public
rows.description: Detects cases where row level security (RLS) has not been enabled on tables in schemas exposed to PostgREST
rows.detail: Table \`public.invoices\` is public, but RLS has not been enabled.

rows.name: rls_references_user_metadata
rows.title: RLS references user metadata
rows.description: Detects when Supabase Auth user_metadata is referenced insecurely in a row level security (RLS) policy.
rows.detail: Table \`public.org_settings\` has a row level security policy \`org_settings_select\` that references Supabase Auth \`user_metadata\`. \`user_metadata\` is editable by end users and should never be used in a security context.

rows.name: rls_policy_always_true
rows.title: RLS Policy Always True
rows.description: Detects RLS policies that use overly permissive expressions like \`USING (true)\` or \`WITH CHECK (true)\` for UPDATE, DELETE, or INSERT operations. SELECT policies with \`USING (true)\` are intentionally excluded as this pattern is often used deliberately for public read access.
rows.detail: Table `public.documents` has an RLS policy `documents_update` for `UPDATE` that allows unrestricted access (both USING and WITH CHECK are always true). This effectively bypasses row-level security for authenticated.

rows.name: rls_policy_always_true
rows.title: RLS Policy Always True
rows.description: Detects RLS policies that use overly permissive expressions like \`USING (true)\` or \`WITH CHECK (true)\` for UPDATE, DELETE, or INSERT operations. SELECT policies with \`USING (true)\` are intentionally excluded as this pattern is often used deliberately for public read access.
rows.detail: Table `public.orgs` has an RLS policy `orgs_insert` for `INSERT` that allows unrestricted access (WITH CHECK clause is always true). This effectively bypasses row-level security for authenticated.
